spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the Kephalaia Teaching Layer

---

**¶1:** Divine Wisdom is the power that shall descend and unite itself with those being regenerated. [GAP-1] It too is one among the divine powers, [GAP-2] and many divine powers attend it. [GAP-3] When it enters within the natural man — the external selfhood of inherited nature — and binds the evil proprium with its five spiritual faculties, it establishes its five faculties upon the proprium throughout the five regions [GAP-4: REVIEW of the] external man.

**¶2:** [GAP-5: REVIEW Thus], now, where does it dwell? For the proprium is restrained within the natural man! Yet I perceive how insurrections of evil arise there despite its bondage, from time to time.

**¶3:** If then it is a great divine power, unchanging and immeasurable, how could it descend and manifest within the confinement of the natural mind?

**¶4:** [GAP-6] Divine Wisdom is holy, and it is pure; [GAP-7] how can it dwell amid the defilement of the natural man?

**¶5:** Fourthly: If truly Divine Wisdom exists within those being regenerated, why is its likeness not displayed to us outwardly, as it truly is?

---

**¶11:** The entire system of falsity — when the adversary of wisdom constructed it — was constructed after the likeness of the human form. The governing principle of the inverted cosmos is the origin of the external appearances of truth. Its connective support is the framework of those appearances. Its receptive center is the five faculties spread open, which [GAP-8: are the interior structure] of the external appearances. Its structural supports are all the discrete degrees of apparent spiritual order. Its central point of connection is the sphere of spiritual knowledges and the ordered cycles of influx. And also, the regions [GAP-9: REVIEW that] extend from its center to its generative seat are [GAP-10] the extensions reaching from the sphere of knowledges to the four quarters of the whole spiritual world. Its generative powers are the three natural degrees that lie beneath, [GAP-11] resting upon the summit of the sustaining foundation. Its [GAP-12] from the [GAP-13] to the ground upon which the sustaining foundation [GAP-14: REVIEW stands] firm. Its lower supports and its base [GAP-15: are] the lowest boundary, and the entire region that belongs [GAP-16] to them.

**¶12:** Its will is human selfhood. Its vital sustenance is natural affections of earthly desire. Its understanding is the intellectual thoughts that [GAP-17: REVIEW move freely] through the rational faculty. Its purifying power is natural knowledges that move within the waters of truth. Its faculty of discrimination is the lowest sensual affections that creep upon the natural mind. Its outermost boundary is the enclosing wall that [GAP-18: ... which] surrounds the piercing force and the great self-love. Its [GAP-19] is the containing forms of that consuming self-love. Its [GAP-20] belongs to falsity from evil. Its bitter falsity is the [GAP-21: ... Its] great interior channel is the breadth of the great [GAP-22] of the spiritual worlds. Its pathways of spiritual life [GAP-23] are all the sources and origins of truth. Its [GAP-24: perception ...] Its foundation is its [GAP-25: ...]

---

**¶13:** This is how each of the spiritual realms has been brought into correspondence with the whole. Five divine powers are fastened within it. [GAP-26] They are its animating soul and its life. [GAP-27] The natural selfhood is in a state of evil. [GAP-28] The Divine Active Power and the Divine Manifestation [GAP-29] are the five vigilant guardians who never cease.

**¶14:** It has [GAP-30] the Guardian of Intelligence — the faculty of higher understanding that is [GAP-31] in the spiritual world of understanding that is above all. It has [GAP-32] the whole [GAP-33] of the heavenly powers that are within [GAP-34] the domain of the great Principle of Honor — which is reflective thought that dwells within the seventh degree of spiritual order. It has humbled [GAP-35] also the Unbreakable Truth, which is the faculty of interior perception [GAP-36] from {GAP-37} it has given [GAP-38] on account of self-love [GAP-39: ... It has] also appointed the Principle of Glorification, which is the deliberative will [GAP-40: and] the faculty of patient endurance over the three essential forms: that of understanding, that of love, and that of truth. It has handed over to it the [GAP-41] tendency to do evil. [GAP-42] the Sustaining Foundation, which is contemplative wisdom [GAP-43] the ground of wisdom in the [GAP-44] which is the lowest degree. It has established this power as [GAP-45] the ground of all being [GAP-46: below...]

---

**¶15:** Furthermore: The Divine Manifestation refined from them five intellectual faculties of spiritual life. Also, the calling-forth of truth and the reception of truth were established there. Now they constituted six powers of the Divine Active Principle, together with the six powers of the Celestial Human!

**¶16:** Further: The Divine Manifestation placed within them the great faculty of Wisdom — which is the Pillar of Divine Truth, the Perfect Human.

**¶17:** Furthermore: The Divine Word in its first revelation was set there — which is the image of living truth, of utterance and reception.

**¶18:** It has fortified these ordered provinces, those above and those below [GAP-47], so that each one shall be secure within the circuit of its domain of governance, so that neither insurrection of evil nor treachery of falsity may arise within its domain.

---

**¶19:** And look, perceive! The Guardian of Intelligence is established firmly in the great faculty of understanding, in the province above the containment of the bound evils, for it brings to nothing all the obscurity of spiritual death. And a treachery occurred, and an insurrection! The evil proprium brought forth premature offspring — it entangled itself with the soul. It became mixed with the wisdom that it had expelled toward the image of the Divine Manifestation. It went [GAP-48] into the third degree of spiritual order that is above the domain [GAP-49: of] the Guardian of Intelligence. From that place also it entangled with the wisdom. It was separated and descended into what is barren and what is fluid in the natural mind. It fashioned perceptions upon the barren natural ground; but in the sea of sensual knowledge it immediately took form and raised a great insurrection within that sensual realm.

**¶20:** Again, look, perceive! The great Principle of Honor, which is reflective thought, stands in the third degree of spiritual order. It is made [GAP-50] to contend against wrath. And an insurrection occurred! A treachery and an anger arose in its domain. The guardian truths of the spiritual degrees, which descended into the natural mind within its domain — they committed all the deeds of treachery. They have revealed the arts of the natural world and have uncovered to people the interior mysteries of the heavenly degrees. An insurrection occurred, and a destruction, upon the natural mind [GAP-51] through it.

**¶21:** The Unbreakable Truth [GAP-52] is the fulfillment of interior perception. It is established firmly upon [GAP-53] and a treachery occurred in its domain — the occasion when the premature offspring of evil fell into the natural mind. They fashioned the primal will and the primal understanding. They begat them so as to reign through them in the world. They fashioned every object of self-love upon the natural mind. The entire world was filled by their concupiscence.

**¶22:** Once again: In the domain of the great Principle of Glorification — which is the great deliberative will, the power that exercises authority over the three cycles of spiritual process — a disturbance occurred, and an affliction, for [GAP-54: the faculties were] pained and oppressed within the three natural degrees. After the Divine Manifestation displayed its image, the paths of ascent closed to their [GAP-55] and their elevation was impeded by them. [GAP-56] The understanding, the truth, and the love ascend through them.

**¶23:** Once again: In the domain of the Sustaining Foundation, the power that humbles [GAP-57] the insurrection of the abysses of evil below — [GAP-58] was bent, and the fastenings beneath were loosened [GAP-59] in the ground of all below.

---

**¶24:** On account of the upheaval that occurred in the domain of the Guardian of Intelligence, the Pillar of Divine Truth came forth; as it [GAP-60] became the helper of the Guardian of Intelligence. It bore up under all burdens of the spiritual order.

**¶25:** Conversely, because of the treachery and the insurrection that occurred in the domain of the great Principle of Honor — which is the guardian truths that descended from the heavenly degrees into the natural mind — four angelic powers were called upon against them. They bound the fallen guardian truths with an eternal chain, in the prison of those in spiritual darkness. They obliterated their offspring from the natural mind.

**¶26:** Then, again, the premature offspring descended within the domain of the Unbreakable Truth and begat the primal will and the primal understanding; because of that great treachery which occurred, and the mystery of wickedness, the Divine Word was sent [GAP-61] with the prayer of the five divine powers. It assumed them [GAP-62] from the premature evils. It fastened them beneath the [GAP-63] the understanding of the primal will.

**¶27:** Also, because of the upheaval that occurred in these three natural degrees, and in that the paths were hindered and the sources of understanding, truth, and love were impeded, the Divine Word cast itself down. It assumed the primal understanding; and it straightened the channels of understanding, truth, and love. It opened the sources for them, and it set in order the path of their ascent.

**¶28:** Once [GAP-64: REVIEW again]: Since the ground beneath the Sustaining Foundation was loosened from the fastenings that [GAP-65] — because of this too the Divine Word went down, assuming the primal understanding until it reached that lowest place. It set in order and strengthened the fastenings beneath. It returned, [GAP-66: REVIEW ascending] up to its [GAP-67] and rest.

---

**¶29:** Look upon all these domains of governance throughout the ordered spiritual world, the ones in which these great divine powers are sovereign, watching over them [GAP-68]. Insurrections have occurred, and treacheries, within them. The [GAP-69] within them from time to time, with great humiliation, until they humbled the powers of the adversary.

**¶30:** So also is this natural man! A mighty divine power lives here, even if the form is small in its stature. Nevertheless, the evil proprium dwells within, and the inherited nature that is lodged in it. Certainly it is cruel, with great cunning; until Divine Wisdom finds how to humble this natural selfhood, and drive it [GAP-70: REVIEW according to] its own purpose.

**¶31:** Just so, in the domains of its great kindred powers — those who are sovereign in the spiritual order — within them, in the great cosmic form, upheaval and treachery occurred from time to time. So also is the domain of Divine Wisdom, which is the external natural man. The evil proprium raises [GAP-71: REVIEW up], from time to time, its agitations within the natural man.

**¶32:** The powers of wisdom are good. The beginning and the end are unveiled to them. All that they do is done with righteous judgment. Indeed, because of this they may permit the adversary to initiate falsity, and accomplish its pleasure for a moment. Then they seize [GAP-72] — for they have acted first with a righteous judgment.

**¶33:** These divine powers, in that [GAP-73] they are great and mighty. And each one of them is enclosed and hard-pressed within the place wherein it is established — like perceptions holding fast to their deepest taproot of life. So also this is how each one of them holds to its taproot of life in the spiritual world, according to the nature of the place in which it is set, bearing up until [GAP-74]...

---

**¶34:** The spiritual world is established firm, being ordered [GAP-75] by the five powers of the Divine Active Principle throughout all its members [GAP-76]. The evil proprium took the natural man out from [GAP-77: REVIEW the] natural ground [GAP-78: and] constructed it in its members. It took the external form from the five forms of falsity and evil. The evil proprium constructed the external man. Yet the soul — the interior life — it took from the five radiant divine powers.

**¶35:** The evil proprium bound the soul in the five members of the external form. It bound the understanding in the deepest foundation; the reflective thought in the connective structure; the interior perception in the channels of life; the deliberative will in the substance; and the contemplative wisdom in the outermost covering.

**¶36:** The evil proprium set fast its own five powers in opposition: its dark understanding upon the understanding of the soul; its dark thought upon the thought of the soul; its dark perception upon the perception of the soul; its dark will upon the will of the soul; its dark wisdom upon the wisdom of the soul. It placed its five agents and authorities upon the five faculties of the soul, which it had drawn in and bound within the natural man.

**¶37:** The soul assumed falsity and forgetfulness. It forgot its essential nature and its origin and its kindred — knowing not the door of the place from which to pray to the Divine, nor how to call upward. It became hostile to its Father [GAP-79] against itself, being wicked [GAP-80] its own wisdom [GAP-81]...

---

**¶38:** Divine Wisdom comes and finds the soul [GAP-82] assuming it within the [GAP-83] its wisdom [GAP-84] it shall become for it [GAP-85] the bonds [GAP-86] the faculties within the natural man. It shall loosen the understanding of the soul and release it from the deepest foundation of falsity. It shall release the thought of the soul from the connective structure; and so bind the thought [GAP-87: REVIEW of the evil proprium within] the connective structure. It shall release the perception of the soul from the channel; and so bind the perception of evil in the channel. It shall loosen the will of the soul, and release it from the substance of falsity; and so bind the will of evil in the substance. It shall release the wisdom of the soul from the outermost covering; and bind the wisdom of evil in the outermost covering.

**¶39:** This is how it shall release the faculties of the soul, and make them free from the five members of the evil proprium. Conversely, these five members of evil, which were loose, it shall bind them.

**¶40:** It shall set right the faculties of the soul; form and purify them, and construct a regenerated person of them, a child of righteousness. [GAP-88: REVIEW And] when [GAP-89: REVIEW it] fashions and constructs and purifies the regenerated person, then it shall bring forth five great living faculties out from the five great divine faculties. And it places them in the members of the regenerated person. It shall place its understanding, which is love, in the understanding of the regenerated person. Also, the thought, which is faith, it shall place in the thought of the regenerated person, whom it shall purify. Its perception, which [GAP-90: REVIEW is perfection, it shall place] in the perception of the regenerated person. Its will, which [GAP-91: REVIEW is] patience, it shall place in the will of the regenerated person. Also, wisdom, which is its contemplation, in the contemplation of the regenerated person. It shall make the image of the interior word pure from the word of evil; and it adds to it its own word, so that its [GAP-92] becomes nourishment and strength [GAP-93]...

---

**¶41:** Now, when it shall perfect [GAP-94: ... the twelve] faculties. This [GAP-95: is how] its wisdom. Its [GAP-96] becomes righteous, as it perfects [GAP-97]... While formerly the person was running [GAP-98] but instead of this, now the person runs [GAP-99] the road and the path and the [GAP-100] also [GAP-101: REVIEW the person ascends] to the heights, to the great heavenly kingdoms [GAP-102] thus the proprium is bound in the [GAP-103] and its concupiscence, its [GAP-104] its foolishness in these five members of the natural man [GAP-105] the dark spirit is imprisoned with them in bondage and in severe misery.

**¶42:** Also, the regenerated person reigns by love, by faith, by perfection, by patience, and by wisdom. Yet, the sovereign [GAP-106] is Divine Wisdom, the power that is sovereign over the totality. It reigns over all according to its own purpose. While the faculties [GAP-107], thus evil is imprisoned. Still, Divine Wisdom is sovereign, and yet an affliction may arise in the natural man from time to time.

**¶43:** There are occasions when the evil proprium shall rise up with its foolishness; and it disturbs contemplation, and it clouds the wisdom and the understanding of the person. It causes truth to be split into doubt, and the person utters some foolish words and some [GAP-108]...

**¶45:** The evil proprium rises again, another time, from contemplation to the deliberative will. It takes patience from the person, and bestows faintheartedness and hurt. [GAP-109] A battle and a war shall arise between Divine Wisdom and the evil proprium in the deliberative will [GAP-110]...

**¶46:** The evil proprium shall rise [GAP-111] and clothe the person with concupiscence and vanity and pride.

**¶47:** The evil proprium shall rise — the thought of spiritual death — to the person's thought. It shall [GAP-112] a vanity; and it causes faith and truth to depart.

**¶49:** The evil proprium shall rise up and assume the person's understanding; and disturb the understanding, which formerly was calm. It shall disrupt love itself.

**¶50:** Divine Wisdom, which was within, shall disperse from the person [GAP-113]. The person shall be filled by evil spirits; and they deal with [GAP-114: REVIEW the person], dragging hither and thither. [GAP-115] [GAP-116: REVIEW The person] will change and become as if a thought of heaven had its truths plucked away. The person becomes merely natural.

---

**¶52:** So also these guardians of the spiritual order, for they are established [GAP-117] firmly within the ordered whole, but they are not visible. Again, this too is the way of Divine Wisdom, [GAP-118: REVIEW for it is] not visible in the natural man.

**¶53:** Also, corresponding to these outer [GAP-119: REVIEW guardians]: in that while they are great, yet have they contracted themselves. They have [GAP-120], they have become small, to the measure of the task that is apportioned to each one of them. Again, this too is like Divine Wisdom — itself a great power, and exalted — but it is bent over and [GAP-121: REVIEW has] become small, to this little worthless natural selfhood.

**¶54:** [GAP-122: REVIEW Even so] the divine powers in the outer spiritual order: they are transcendent and purified, they are set fast within the mingling of the totality, but are not defiled. [GAP-123: REVIEW This too is like] Divine [GAP-124: REVIEW Wisdom]. While it is placed in its [GAP-125]...

**¶55:** Again, behold the mightiness and the activity of Divine Wisdom: how vast it is over all the domains of the natural man! It stays fast at its post. It shuts off all deliberations of the natural man from the beguilements of evil. It limits them and distributes them rightly. It sets them down according to its own purpose.

**¶56:** Also, it does another work, surpassing and exceeding all these. It bestows a great spirit upon the one chosen for regeneration. Indeed, now you may find this person standing upon the natural ground, rising up in the will and ascending to the Father, the Divine Source of truth — the One who exists and is established above all the things of loss and perishing. Once again, the person may press downward in perception and contemplation, and descend to the realm of falsity, from where all falsity has poured forth. The will shall run and touch everything, as it [GAP-126]...

He shall release the consideration of the soul from the skin; and bin[d] the consideration of the Sin in the skin.
This is how he shall release the members of the soul, and make them free from the five members of Sin. Conversely, these five members of Sin, which were loose, he shall bind them.

He shall set right the members of the soul; form and purify them, and construct a new man of them, a child of righteousness. [And] when [he] fashions and const[r]ucts and purifies the new man; then he shall bring forth five great living members out from the five great memb[ers]. And he places them in the members of the new man. He shall place his m[ind], which is love, in the mind of the new man. Also, the th[oug]ht, which is faith, he shall pl[ace in] the thought of the new man; whom he shall purify. His insight, which [is perfection, he shall place] in the insight of the new man. His counsel, which [is] patience, he shall place in his counsel. Also, [w]isdom, which is his consideration, in the consideration of the new m[an]. He shall make the image of the word pure from the word of Sin; and he adds to it his word, so that his [word] becomes nourisher and strengthener [...]

Now, when he shall perf[ect all the tw]elve members. This [is how ...] and his wisdom. His [word] becomes righteous, as he perf[ects him] While formerly he was running [in error] but instead of this, now he runs [upon] his road and his path and his [ascent] also [he mounts up] to the heights, to the great aeons [of light, and] thus the old man is bound in the [flesh] and his lust, his [wrath] his foolishness in these five members of the bo[dy, and] the dark spirit is imprisoned with them in a bond and in severe misery.

Also, the new man reigns by his love, by hi[s] faith, by his perfection, by his patience, and by his wisdom. Yet, his king [is] the Light Mind, he w[ho is] king over the totality. He re[igns] o[ver it according to] his pleasure. While the members [obey him], thus Sin is imprisoned. Still, the Light Mind is king, and an affliction may arise in the body from t[im]e to time.

There are occasions when Sin shall mount up with its foolishness; and it disturbs the consideration, and it clouds the wisdom and the understanding of the person. It causes truth to be split into doubt in him, and he utters some foo[li]sh words and some [wicked deeds]

Sin mount up again, another time, from the consideration to the counsel. It takes his patience f[rom him], and bestows upon him faint-heartedness and hurt. [...] A battle and a war shall arise (between) the Light Mind and the Sin in the counsel [...]
Sin shall rise [up to his insight] and clothe him with lust and vanity and pride.
Sin shall mount up, the thought of death, to his thought. He shall [conceive] a vanity; and causes his f[ai]th and his truth to le[a]ve him.
(Sin) shall rise up and assume his mind; and disturb his mind, which formerly was calm. It shall disrupt his love

The Mind, who was in him, sh[a]ll disperse from him [and depart] He shall be filled by evil spirits; and they deal with [him], dragging [hi]m hither and thither. [...] [He] will change and become as if a b[i]rd, were its feathers plucked out. He becomes an earthly man.
So al[so] these watch-keepers, for they are set [fast and] fi[rm in] the zone, (but) they are not visible. Again, this too is the way of the Light Mind, [for he is] not visible in the body.

Also, [corr]esponding to th[ese] outer [watch-keepers]: in that while they are great, [y]et have they contorted themselves. They have [humbled themselves], they have become small, to the measure of the task that is apportioned to each o[n]e [of t]hem. Again, this too is like the Mind, himse[lf] a great one, and exalted; but he is bent over and [has] become small, to this little worthless [bo]dy.

[Even so] the gods in the outer [z]one: they are transcendent and purified, they are set [f]a[st in] the mingling of the totality, (but) are not defiled. [This too is like the] Light [Mind]. While he is placed in hi[s body, he is not defiled]

Again, behold the mightiness and the activity of the Light Mind: how vast he is over all the watch-districts of the body! He stays fast at his camp. He shuts off all deliberations of the body from the beguilements of Sin. He limits them and distributes them out. He sets them down at his pleasure.

Also, he does another work, surpassing and ex/ceeding (these). He bestows a great spirit upon the ele/ct one. Indeed, now may you find him, as he stands on the earth, [r]ising up in his heart and ascending to the Father, the G[o]d of truth. He who exists and is established above all the things of loss. [Onc]e again, he may push dow[n] in his insight and his consideration, and descend to the land of Darkness, from where the Darkness has poured forth. His heart shall run and touch everything, as it [pleases]

fills.explanation: The conjunction "For" explains why the Light Mind can assume the saints — because he is one among the gods with many gods attending him; this introduces the supporting description.
The spiritual reading confirms "and" as the conjunction connecting the two parallel statements about the Light Mind being among the gods and many gods being with him.
The temporal marker "Now" is the Kephalaia's standard transitional word introducing the main narrative sequence: "Now, when he enters within the body of the flesh."
The five counsels are set upon the old man in the five limbs of his body — "his" referring to the old man being bound, matching the possessive structure.
The editor's "So" correctly introduces the inferential question that follows from the preceding description of the Light Mind's entry into the body.
The enumeration pattern requires "Thirdly" here, as ¶5 explicitly says "Fourthly" and this is the third question about the Light Mind's nature.
The spiritual reading identifies this as a question about how the pure Mind can endure the body's defilement, requiring an interrogative phrase connecting purity to defilement.
Completes "are the middle" — the stomach and five unfolded ones correspond to the interior/middle section of the cosmic garments, matching the spiritual reading's "interior structure."
The editor's "that" correctly serves as the relative pronoun introducing the clause "that come from his navel to his hip."
The demonstrative "those" parallels the preceding structure: "the parts that come from navel to hip are those that come from the sphere to the corners of the four worlds."
The three earths are both below (in position) and rest upon the head of the Porter, matching the spiritual reading's "resting upon the summit of the sustaining foundation."
In the descending body-cosmos correspondence, between loins and shins the next body part is the thighs, continuing the anatomical mapping of the macrocosmic body.
The thighs extend from the loins (just described as the three earths) downward to the earth where the Porter stands, following the body's descending order.
The editor's "is stood" is a valid stative construction in translated Coptic, describing the Porter's firm establishment upon the earth.

Completes "are the abysses below" — below the Porter's standing point are the abysses of darkness, referenced in ¶23's "uprising of the abysses below," matching the spiritual reading's "lowest boundary."
The spiritual reading confirms "to them" as the completion of "the entire zone that belongs to them," referring to the abysses and lowest regions.
The editor's "fly in" correctly describes what birds do in the air, matching the natural-plane register of this body-cosmos correspondence.
The great intestine corresponds to the breadth of the great sea of the worlds — the cosmic ocean that stretches through the Manichaean cosmos, matching the spiritual reading's "great channel."
The simple copula "are" connects veins to their cosmic correspondence: "His veins are all the springs and wells," matching the chapter's consistent X-is-Y pattern.
The conjunction "For" explains why the five gods are fastened in the cosmic body: because they are its animating soul and life.
Introduces the adversative contrast: though the five gods are the soul/life, "yet the old man is a sinner" — using the chapter's standard term "old man" for the evil proprium.
The adversative "But" transitions from the old man's sinfulness to the countervailing action of the Living Spirit and the Ambassador who establish the guardians.
The Living Spirit and Ambassador "have appointed" the five sleepless guardians to watch over the cosmic body, matching the paragraph's pattern of divine delegation and the chapter's verb usage.
The first deity in the series, the Keeper of Splendour, is "placed" — established in his position in the world of the mind above, following the paragraph's pattern of divine appointments.
The mind is "set" in the world of the mind above, using the chapter's standard verb for establishing divine powers in their positions (cf. "set firm" throughout).
Continues the pattern of divine establishment: "He has set the whole host of the powers of heaven" in the domain of the King of Honour.
The "whole host" of the powers of heaven is a standard expression in the Kephalaia register for the collectivity of heavenly powers gathered under a governing deity.
The heavenly powers are set in "the camp" of the King of Honour — "camp" is the chapter's standard term for a deity's domain (used repeatedly in ¶19–23).

The Adamant of Light is "the insight that comes from above" — paralleling the description of other deities with their faculties and origins, and matching the spiritual reading's directional "from above."
Single-word gap: the Adamant of Light is the insight that comes "from above," indicating the celestial origin of this faculty of interior perception.

Completes "counsel and the patience" — the King of Glory is identified with both the deliberative will (counsel) and patient endurance, matching the spiritual reading's "deliberative will and the faculty of patient endurance."
The King of Glory is given authority over "the powers that do evilness" — the hostile forces in the three earths that the counsel/patience must govern.
Follows the paragraph's pattern where each deity is introduced with "He has [verbed]" — the Porter is the final deity to be set in place.
Connects the two aspects of the Porter's faculty: "the consideration and the wisdom," since consideration and wisdom are closely linked (cf. ¶40 "wisdom, which is his consideration").
The Porter's wisdom is in "the earth which is below" — the Porter/Atlas is associated with the lowest cosmic level, the earth beneath all.
The Porter's defining role is to "bear" the foundation — as the Atlas figure, he carries/supports the worlds from below, matching the spiritual reading's "ground of all being."
The Porter bears the foundation "below the earths" — he supports everything from the lowest position, beneath the three earths described as his loins.
The camps "above and below in the world" encompasses the complete cosmic order that the divine powers have fortified — "in the world" is a standard Kephalaia locative phrase.
Sin "went up" into the third firmament, describing the upward invasion of the expelled light-substance toward the higher cosmic regions.
Completes "watch-tower of" — the third firmament is above the watch-tower of the Keeper of Splendour, his domain of governance.
The King of Honour is "made to contend with wrath" — established to combat the hostile force of anger in his domain, matching the spiritual reading's "contend against wrath."
Completes the full title and identification: "The Adamant of Light, who is the fulfillment" — following the chapter's pattern of identifying each deity with their spiritual faculty.
Completes "upon the earth" — the Adamant of Light guards the earth from above, and the treachery in his camp was the abortions falling to the earth.
The editor's reading "they were" correctly supplies the subject and verb for "pained and oppressed in the three earths," identifying the suffering powers in the King of Glory's domain.
The paths closed to their "springs" echoes ¶27's parallel language: "the paths were hindered and the springs of wind and water and fire were impeded."
The definite article completes "he who humiliates the uprising of the abysses below," identifying the Porter's role as suppressor of the lower insurrections.
The subject of "bent" — "the earth was bent" describes the cosmic earthquake in the Porter's domain, where the earth beneath him buckled and the fastenings loosened.

In the Porter's domain the "earthquake" (¶24) loosened "and shaken" the fastenings — the paired verbs describe structural failure, and "shaken" directly echoes the earthquake motif that links ¶23 to ¶24.
The Pillar of Glory "became the helper" of the Keeper of Splendour — it came forth in response to the earthquake and assumed the role of supporting the cosmic order.
Jesus was sent "with the prayer of the five sons" — the preposition connects Jesus's mission to the invocation of the five divine powers, matching the spiritual reading.
Jesus "assumed them from the abortions" — he rescued the captive light-elements from the premature offspring of evil, matching the spiritual reading's "from the premature evils."
The editor's "again" correctly maintains the chapter's recurring formula "Once again" that introduces each successive watch-district narrative.
The earth was loosened "from the fastenings that held it" — the fastenings had previously held the earth in place, and their loosening prompted Jesus's descent to restore them.
The editor's "he came" correctly describes Jesus's return ascent: "He returned, he came up to his place of rest."
Jesus returned to his "place of rest" — a standard Manichaean expression for the heavenly abode of light to which the redeemer ascends after his salvific descent.
The great gods watch over their zones "at all times" — continuous vigilance is the defining quality of the watchkeepers, matching the "sleepless guardians" description.
Parallels ¶31's "the earthquake and treachery happened from time to time" — the struggles arose repeatedly until the powers of enmity were humbled.
The editor's "according to" correctly renders the Light Mind's governance of the body "according to his pleasure," matching the chapter's repeated formula (cf. ¶42, ¶55).
The editor's "up" correctly completes the phrase "Sin raises up its agitations," matching the chapter's consistent language for Sin's insurrections.
The powers of light "seize it" (the enmity/sin), "for" they have acted with righteous judgement — the pronoun refers to the permitted evil, and "for" introduces the justification.
The pronoun "they" is the subject of "are great and mighty ones": "These gods, in that they are great and mighty ones" — a standard concessive construction.
The gods bear up "till the end" — they sustain their cosmic roles until the eschatological consummation, holding fast to their taproot in the world.
The world is "ordered by the five sons of the Living Spirit" — the preposition identifies the divine agents through whom the cosmic order is established.
The editor's "the" correctly supplies the article: "Sin took this body out from the land" — the definite article specifies the material ground from which the body was fashioned.
Completes "land and constructed": "Sin took this body out from the land and constructed it in its members" — the spiritual reading confirms "and" as the bridge between extraction and construction.
The soul became hostile both to its Father "and against" itself — a double hostility matching the spiritual reading's "against itself," describing the inverted state of the fallen soul.
The soul is "wicked against its own light" — it acts in opposition to its own divine essence, matching the spiritual reading's identification of self-destructive evil.
The editor's "of the Sin in" correctly follows the chapter's systematic pattern: the Light Mind binds each faculty of Sin in the corresponding bodily member as it releases the soul's faculty.
The editor's "And" correctly begins the next clause connecting the construction of the new man to the implantation of the five living members.
The editor's "he" correctly refers to the Light Mind as the agent who fashions and constructs the new man, maintaining the chapter's masculine pronoun convention.
The editor's fill follows the exact pattern established for the other four faculties: identifying the virtue and then placing it in the corresponding member of the new man.
The editor's "is" correctly supplies the copula: "His counsel, which is patience" — matching the identification pattern for all five faculties and their virtues.
The Light Mind's "word" becomes nourisher and strengthener — the preceding sentence describes adding "his word" to the purified image, so the word itself becomes the nourishing power.
Completes "perfect all the twelve members" — the Light Mind perfects the complete set of twelve faculties (five of the soul, five of the new man, plus the word and its image).
Following ¶40's emphasis on purifying and strengthening the word, "His word becomes righteous" describes the perfected state of the interior word after the twelve members are completed.
Completes "perfects him" — referring to the new man: "His word becomes righteous, as he perfects him," where "him" is the new man being brought to completion by the Light Mind.
The contrast between former and present states: "formerly he was running in error, but now he runs upon his road" — error is the state before the Light Mind's perfecting work.
The preposition "upon" connects the person's new direction: "now he runs upon his road and his path" — the righteous way established by the Light Mind's regeneration.
The third term in the triad "his road and his path and his ascent" — building toward GAP-101's mounting up to the heights, the language of spiritual elevation through regeneration.
The editor's "he mounts up" correctly describes the regenerated person's spiritual elevation, using the chapter's standard verb for upward movement (cf. Sin "mounts up" in ¶43–47).
The person ascends to "the great aeons of light" — a standard Manichaean designation for the heavenly kingdoms — "and" then transitions to the binding of the old man.
The old man is "bound in the flesh" — matching the chapter's binding terminology where counsel of Sin is bound in flesh (¶38), and the flesh represents the material body's constraint.
The triad "lust, wrath, foolishness" is the classic triplet of cardinal vices in the Kephalaia's register — corresponding to the three levels of concupiscence, anger, and ignorance.
Completes "body, and" — bridging from the five members of the body to the consequence: "and the dark spirit is imprisoned with them in a bond."
The copula "is" identifies the sovereign: "his king is the Light Mind" — establishing the Light Mind as the supreme ruler over the new man's totality.
While the five members of the new man "obey him" (the Light Mind), Sin is imprisoned — the obedience of the regenerated faculties is what constrains the evil proprium.
The parallel "some foolish words and some wicked deeds" pairs speech and action — the standard doublet in ancient religious instruction for the effects of Sin's disturbance.

Following the ascending progression of Sin's attacks (consideration → counsel → insight → thought → mind), ¶46 describes Sin rising "up to his insight" and clothing the person with lust — the Adamant/insight level is associated with lust throughout the chapter.
At the thought level, Sin causes the person to "conceive a vanity" — the verb fits the thought-faculty context and the production of false ideation that displaces faith and truth.

The Light Mind "shall disperse from him and depart" — the double verb emphasizes the completeness of the withdrawal when Sin conquers all five faculties, leaving the person to be filled by evil spirits.
The editor's "him" correctly identifies the person as the object: the evil spirits "deal with him, dragging him hither and thither."
The editor's "He" correctly supplies the subject pronoun for the person who "will change and become as if a bird were its feathers plucked out."

Combines the chapter's two established phrases "set fast" (¶36, ¶54) and "set firm" into the emphatic doublet "set fast and firm in the zone" — a standard Coptic paired construction for emphasis on divine establishment.
The editor's "for he is" correctly draws the parallel: just as the watch-keepers are not visible in the zone, so the Light Mind is "not visible in the body."
The editor's "watch-keepers" matches the chapter's consistent term for the five sons of the Living Spirit who guard the cosmic zones, used repeatedly throughout.

The second verb in the sequence — they "contorted themselves, they have humbled themselves, they have become small" — matches the chapter's vocabulary of humiliation and the Mind's self-contraction into the body.
The editor's "has" correctly forms the perfect tense: "he is bent over and has become small" — describing the Mind's completed self-diminishment to fit the body.
The editor's "Even so" correctly introduces the final parallel comparison: just as the outer gods are transcendent and undefiled, so too the Light Mind in the body.
The editor's phrase matches the chapter's recurring comparative formula (cf. ¶53: "this too is like the Mind") drawing the parallel between the outer gods and the Light Mind.
The editor's "Mind" correctly identifies the entity: "the Light Mind" is the chapter's consistent natural-plane term for Divine Wisdom throughout all 56 paragraphs.

fills.explanation: Completes "his body, he is not defiled" — the closing parallel of ¶54 states that just as the outer gods are set in the mingling but not defiled, so the Light Mind is placed in the body but remains pure.
The chapter's final word echoes its recurring motif of sovereign purpose: the heart runs and touches everything "as it pleases" — cf. ¶30, ¶42, ¶55 where governance is exercised "at his pleasure."
